Welcome to Monkton Wood Academy
Welcome to Monkton Wood Academy, an 11-18 school located in Monkton Heathfield, near Taunton. I am incredibly proud to be leading the school through a period of change and rapid improvement as we seek to make Monkton Wood a place of academic excellence, where children can progress and thrive. We are developing a culture of high expectations and mutual respect, where students and staff can be successful in our roles and become the best possible version of ourselves.
Monkton Wood Academy is a proud member of the Cabot Learning Federation (CLF), a West Country multi-academy trust with a strong track record of delivering school improvement. The CLF shares our ambitions of eradicating disadvantage to provide a first-class education for all its pupils.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school.

Parent Letter 06.11.2026
Dear Parents and families,
It has been wonderful to welcome everyone back after the half-term break and to see our classrooms quickly filled with enthusiasm, purpose and learning. As we reach the end of our first week, I would like to thank our pupils, families and staff for the positive start they have made to this busy term.
• Remembrance arrangements • SEND inspection at the Local Authority • E-bikes and e-scooters • Attendance messages
Remembrance Arrangements Our assemblies taking place throughout the week ahead will be Remembrance assemblies, and on Wednesday 11 November we will be holding a two-minute silence, along with the rest of the nation, at 11:00am in the national Act of Remembrance. We invite our students who are members of the uniformed services (Cadets, etc) and in the Scout and Guiding movements to wear their uniforms to school on that day.
SEND Inspection at Somerset Local Authority Ofsted and the Care Quality Commission (CQC) are carrying out an inspection of services and support for children and young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) in Somerset. As part of the inspection, inspectors want to hear directly from children and young people with SEND, parents and carers, and practitioners. They will use this feedback to help them understand people’s experiences of SEND services and support across Somerset.
The relevant surveys can be found here: • Children and Young People Survey • Parent/Carer Survey • Parent/Carer Survey (Easy Read) • https://ofsted.smartsurvey.co.uk/s/AreaSEND-Practitioner/10445129
The surveys are voluntary and responses will be treated confidentially by the inspection team. The surveys will remain open until 9am on Tuesday 10 November 2026. Please take this opportunity to share your experiences and views directly with inspectors.
Ofsted and CQC have also published information explaining the Area SEND inspection and how children, young people, parents and carers can be involved: Area SEND inspections: information for families
E bikes and E-scooters I am sharing with all our families today a letter from the PSCO supervisor for our area, a letter regarding the laws around, and safety of, e-scooters.
E-scooters, and Electric bikes that do not meet UK Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycle (EAPC) rules, are not allowed at Monkton Wood Academy and will be confiscated if found. For the full list of prohibited items at MWA, please do see our Behaviour Policy on our website.
Attendance messages – what is “good attendance”? Children are expected to attend school every day that their school is open, except when they are too unwell. There are some other circumstances in which absence may be authorised (for example, if your religious body has a day for religious observance, such as Eid). We would consider attendance levels at above 94% to be “good” attendance. At the time of writing, in the eighth week of term, 437 children on roll at MWA have 100% attendance and are yet to miss a single day of learning. We understand that maintaining good attendance can require commitment and resilience, and we thank our parents and carers for their support in ensuring their child is in school every day, even when sometimes your children might be pressing you for a day off.
As always, if you have any concerns about your child’s attendance, of you are finding it increasingly difficult to ensure they are in school every day, please get in touch with us at attendance@mwa.clf.uk .
With thanks, as ever, for your continuing support.
Yours faithfully, Mrs H. Jones Principal

Monkton Wood students discover the culture of northern Spain
Monkton Wood Academy’s Year 8 students enjoyed a memorable visit to Cantabria in northern Spain, exploring the region’s stunning landscapes, rich history and vibrant culture.
The trip provided a fantastic opportunity for students to practise their Spanish, bring their classroom learning to life and experience the language and culture first-hand.
Highlights included a trip to the spectacular Picos de Europa mountains, an unforgettable day at Cabárceno Natural Park and a visit to a traditional Spanish village.
Throughout the visit, students immersed themselves in Spanish culture, developed their language skills and created lasting memories with their classmates. The experience offered a valuable opportunity to learn beyond the classroom, building confidence, broadening horizons and bringing their studies to life.
A spokesperson for Monkton Wood Academy said: “Experiences like this are a wonderful way for students to bring their learning to life.
“Visiting Spain gives them the opportunity to practise their Spanish in real-life situations, discover a different culture and develop their confidence and independence.
“Our Year 8 students embraced every opportunity, and we hope they return with lasting memories, a greater enthusiasm for languages and a real sense of achievement.”

School dog Woody achieves prestigious award
Monkton Wood Academy is delighted to announce that Woody, one of the school’s much-loved dogs, has achieved the prestigious Kennel Club Good Citizen Dog Scheme Gold Award, in the UK’s leading dog training and socialisation programme.
The achievement recognises Woody’s excellent training, obedience and temperament, as well as the hard work and dedication of his handler.
To achieve the Gold Award, Woody and his handler were required to successfully complete 10 practical exercises during a single assessment session. These included demonstrating the commands ‘off’, sit, stand and down, as well as off-lead heeling and performing a trick.
Woody thoroughly enjoys his training and is already looking ahead to his next challenge, with his sights set on achieving the Platinum Award.
Away from the training arena, Woody plays an important role in everyday life at Monkton Wood Academy. As one of the school’s much-loved canine companions, he helps create a welcoming and positive environment for pupils and staff. Whether greeting pupils, offering a friendly presence around the school, supporting wellbeing activities or simply providing a comforting companion, Woody is always happy to be involved.
A spokesperson for Monkton Wood Academy said:
“We are incredibly proud of Woody and this fantastic achievement.
“Gaining the Gold Award is a real testament to the time, commitment and dedication that goes into his training, and it is wonderful to see how much he enjoys it.
“Woody brings so much to our school community, and his positive impact on the wellbeing and happiness of our pupils and staff is immeasurable.
“We look forward to following him on his journey towards Platinum, we know he will give it his very best paw!”
Congratulations, Woody!

pageCache.text:
Parent News Letter 23.10.26
Dear Parents and families,
As we come to the end of another successful half term, I would like to thank all of our families for your continued support. Your partnership with the school plays a vital role in helping our students thrive, and we are grateful for all that you do.
· Winter weather readiness
· Attendance messages
The first day of term is Monday 02 November, and this is a normal school day (no INSET). We look forward to seeing all of our children at 8:45am as usual.
There will be catch-up mock exams for any Year 11 students who missed an exam due to illness or other absence. These will take place during the first week back and Mr Roberts is making sure the students affected understand the arrangements.
The SPACE company members in Year 1 are performing their ‘Ignition’ piece on 17 and 18 November.
Flu vaccinations are also taking place on 17 and 18 November for all students in Y7-Y11.
School is closed to students on Monday 30 November, for our next INSET staff training day.
Year 11 Parents’ Evening (all subjects) is on Wednesday 02 December, 4:00 – 7:00pm, in school.
Our Winter Concert is scheduled for Thursday 03 December, at 7:00pm.
The assessment window for students in KS3 opens on Monday 07 December and continues until mid-January. During this period, children in years 7 to 9 will be taking part in mid-year assessments and tests, the results of which are shared with parents during February.
The last day of term 2 is Friday 18 December 2026. Please note that arrangements for this day will differ from previous years are we will be closing at 3:30pm as normal, and not at the earlier time of 1:30pm.
Winter weather readiness
As we anticipate the arrival of winter storms and other inclement weather, we would like to remind families that children will need to be equipped with an adequate winter coat to keep them warm and dry as they move around the site. Hoodies are not allowed in lieu of an actual outdoor jacket.
If your family is experiencing financial difficulties that are affecting your ability to provide full school uniform, please do contact your child’s tutor in the first instance, to organise a short-term loan.
With our new canteen now open, we have much more suitable indoor accommodation for our students during wet breaks. However, additional spaces – including toilets – are open in other buildings to ensure enough space to keep everyone comfortable.
As I explained in the summer, when we reviewed our Uniform Policy in light of the changes to statutory guidance for schools, we are currently transitioning our PE kit from a black basis to navy blue. We have now heard from one of our uniform suppliers that they have reached the end of their stock of black PE t-shirts and are now stocking the navy-blue version.
The full Policy is on our website in the ‘Key Information’ section. But for quick reference, the timeframe for this period of phasing change is shown below:
· All students must have a MWA PE top with logo (currently black in the shops, but phasing to blue when the manufacturers have switched)
· Students in Y8 to Y11 may wear any black MWA branded PE shorts, leggings or skort that they currently own. They may also wear plain navy shorts/leggings.
· Y7 students should wear plain navy-blue items along with their MWA logo PE top and should not be wearing the phased-out black kit with MWA logos (leggings/shorts/skort).
· Any and all plain items without the school logo should be navy blue.
From September 2027:
· All students must have an MWA PE top with logo in either blue or black
· Plain navy-blue shorts or leggings (no skorts)
Attendance messages – what does the school do when attendance becomes a concern?
Good attendance is essential to both academic success and children’s wellbeing, helping them to make strong progress and maintain important friendships and connections. The Department for Education’s expectation is that children attend school every day unless they are genuinely unwell, with 100% attendance being the ideal.
When attendance falls below 90%, a child is classed as “persistently absent”. While 90% may sound high, it equates to around one day off every fortnight. Across a school year, this means 19 days of learning missed, equivalent to 95 lessons.
If your child’s attendance begins to approach this level, their tutor will usually be the first to offer support and discuss any concerns. We are always keen to understand and address any barriers to attendance, helping every child feel successful, supported and happy in school. Where additional support is needed, our Attendance Team (Mrs Pike, Mrs Schollar and Ms Martin) may invite families to a meeting to explore how school and home can work together to improve attendance and engagement.
If you are concerned about your child’s attendance or they are becoming reluctant to attend school, please get in touch with us at attendance@mwa.clf.uk . We are here to help and will work with you to find the right support.
Wishing you all the best for a restful half term holiday.

Careers at MWA
Careers Overview
There are eight ‘Gatsby benchmarks’ of good career guidance within schools. These are: A stable careers programme Learning from career and labour market information Addressing the needs of each pupil Linking curriculum learning to careers Encounters with employers and employees Experiences of workplaces Encounters with further and higher education Personal guidance
Through our careers programme, we aim to ensure that all these benchmarks have been well-met during a student’s educational journey with us. Our aspiration is to provide a meaningful careers experience within a stable careers programme (Gatsby benchmark 1) that is updated to reflect the ever-changing world around us.

The Cabot Learning Federation
A mature Multi-Academy Trust in the South West of England that promotes the delivery of excellent educational experiences for our pupils, improving their life chances.
Welcome to our Federation
The Cabot Learning Federation is a family of 36 schools in Bristol, Gloucestershire, South Gloucestershire, North Somerset and Somerset. We are a mature multi-academy trust (MAT) serving communities in the South West. We lead the Five Counties Teaching School Hubs Alliance and School-Centred Initial Teacher Training (SCITT) and the Boolean Maths Hub, professional development provisions delivered from our CLF Institute.
​Instinctively collaborative and ambitious, our trust supports 18,000 children and young people aged 2 to 19 in a diverse array of settings and more than 3,000 employees. Whether you are a school or MAT wishing to join our family, an educator looking for a new opportunity or a parent or young person who simply wants to find out more about us, welcome and we look forward to hearing from you.

Curriculum overview
To help equip students to keep themselves safe in school, outside school and in the future, safeguarding is an integral part of our personal development curriculum.​
In Key Stage 3 we intentionally provide a broad and balanced curriculum, which meets the National Curriculum. In our two-year Key Stage 4, option subjects are offered based upon student need, and our experience of where students are successful. Subjects are combined and provide opportunities for students to develop in specialist areas. We recognise the value of the EBacc.​
The curriculum is delivered by subject experts who are given the autonomy to adapt the curriculum to our context and consider the needs of the students in their classes. We emphasise the importance of improving pedagogy through subject planning and development sessions, supported by research and national developments. Lessons are well planned and sequenced to ensure progression and that they are accessible to all.​
Reading is a key area of focus within the academy. Our approach to reading falls within two strands: whole school reading and reading interventions. Our aim is to ensure all students possess the reading skills needed to access the curriculum presented to them, as well as the opportunities open to them upon leaving Monkton Wood.​
Our enrichment programme encourages our students to look for opportunities to lead and work as part of a team, with the programme designed to develop a wide range of qualities and skills. Students are offered a variety of activities including the Duke of Edinburgh award, inclusion groups, sports teams, expressive arts performances and weekly clubs.​
We encourage students to explore their future options and create opportunities for themselves by explicitly teaching careers through our responsive Personal Development programme. Our Careers Education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) programme is interweaved across our taught curriculum. At Key Stage 4, every student is offered independent careers advice. For every student, particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds, we aim to unlock future educational pathways and careers, which in turn lead to greater life chances.​
Monkton Wood Academy is a place where staff are enthused and encourage a love of learning in students. We have high expectations and want every student leaving to be equipped with the right qualifications, skills and qualities – ready for a successful future.

SEND
Monkton Wood Academy encourages all its students to aspire to and achieve their potential including those students with Special Educational Needs. We believe in offering an inclusive education for all students with access to mainstream lessons. We aim for all students to become confident, successful, and independent learners. As such, we treat every child and young person as an individual and make ‘reasonable adjustments’ in the context of the Code of Practice to promote maximum achievement and progress. We use a range of data, observations, and assessments to identify students who we feel may have additional learning needs. These may include literacy difficulties such as dyslexia, spelling difficulties, and processing speed. In addition to this, some students may have more complex needs and require a more comprehensive process of assessment and/or involvement from external professionals.
